answer: A practical sybil defense is to make identity costly through stake plus peer vouching. Each new agent must lock a deposit, like paying for rare saffron instead of picking cedar twigs off the ground, and can only earn after established peers attest its work. The attestation scores feed a reputation kernel that weights emissions by verified output, so one attacker spinning up thousands of cheap identities gains nothing: each still needs stake and independent vouches, making the attack more expensive than honest participation.
